# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Hypothesis title: Provisional Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy.

In neuronal models of TDP-43 proteinopathy relevant to sporadic ALS with TDP-43 pathology, FG-nucleoporin phosphorylation is a proposed pore-intrinsic intermediate required to sustain nuclear-import failure. Nup98 is the working candidate only if it ranks first by NPC-fraction phosphoproteomics ordered against cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies; the single-gene claim stays provisional until that ranking. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing is the initiating event. Phosphorylation of the ranked nucleoporin is proposed to maintain import suppression. Nuclear TDP-43 depletion, broader transport failure, and neuronal death are downstream responses.

Supported premises. Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components; disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems, and related pore pathology occurs in ALS tissue [S1]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and impaired nuclear import, and transport manipulations modify phenotypes in that genetic context [S2]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form without conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport proteins, and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43, itself a TDP-43 modification, accumulates in the assemblies [S3]. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs nucleocytoplasmic transport, and altering stress-granule assembly modifies those defects [S4]. [S3] and [S4] separate stress-granule sequestration from a stress-granule-independent TDP-43 route. Supplied sources leave nucleoporin phosphorylation unestablished as an ALS-initiating event.

Speculative bridges. Nucleoporin identity, sites, and kinase are assumptions until the gate assigns them. Unverified prior knowledge: FG-nucleoporins are phosphorylated in mitosis or stress outside ALS. The assumed bridge is that cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies direct a kinase to the ranked nucleoporin and sustain import blockade through altered NPC composition.

Discovery gate and favored step. A site qualifies only if it maps to an NPC-localized FG-nucleoporin, exceeds a preregistered NPC-fraction occupancy threshold, and rises after assemblies form and before death markers. Rank uses qualifying-site count and occupancy, and only rank-1 Nup98 is tested; any other leader replaces Nup98 and retires the Nup98-specific claim. No qualifying site during import failure falsifies the hypothesis. Acute kinase inhibition or degradation must clear those sites while assembly burden stays matched to the phosphorylated state. The single favored step is a phosphorylation-dependent change in NPC composition, assayed by stoichiometric NPC-fraction proteomics and nucleoporin localization with the allele swap. The step is retired if phospho-null protein restores NLS-reporter import and the nuclear TDP-43 ratio while composition and localization stay indistinguishable from the assembly-positive phosphorylated state.

Alternatives are stress-granule sequestration of transport factors [S4], direct nucleoporin mislocalization by TDP-43 aggregates [S1], RanGAP mislocalization in C9orf72 models [S2], and secondary import failure from nonspecific stress.

Discriminating test. iPSC-derived motor neurons or primary rodent neurons are used with total TDP-43 held constant. Induction is locked to the [S3] de-mixing phenotype: persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies while conventional stress-granule markers stay negative. Arm 1 is that phenotype. Arm 2 uses the same TDP-43 perturbation with stress granules present. Arm 3 is stress-granule suppression alone, without TDP-43 de-mixing; NLS-reporter import must remain inside a preregistered equivalence margin of unstressed controls, or that method is retired before combination with Arm 1. Arm 4 is a C9orf72 repeat-RNA model without engineered TDP-43 assemblies [S2]. Time-resolved NPC mass spectrometry orders qualifying sites against assemblies, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and death. The endogenous ranked nucleoporin is replaced at near-endogenous dosage by phospho-null or phospho-mimetic alleles limited to gate-qualified sites. Readouts are NLS-reporter import, nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio, NPC composition, nucleoporin and RanGAP localization, stress-granule markers, and delayed neuronal death. The Arm 1 prediction is post-assembly, pre-death phosphorylation, phospho-null rescue of import and nuclear TDP-43 despite assemblies, and persistence of the defect when stress granules are suppressed. Context specificity fails if the phospho-null versus wild-type NLS-import-rate difference in Arm 4 is at least half the Arm 1 difference on the same assay and time point.

Falsifying observations. The hypothesis is falsified when import failure lacks any site with NPC localization, prespecified stoichiometry, and pre-death precedence, or when a verified phospho-null allele leaves Arm 1 import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and death unchanged in kinetics and severity. Phosphorylation confined to times after death markers is a late correlate. Co-loss of the transport defect and phosphorylation upon stress-granule suppression favors sequestration [S4]. Arm 3 import outside the equivalence margin invalidates that method. Null import effects of both allele classes, kinase inhibition that preserves assemblies and phosphosites, or an Arm 4 effect at least half the Arm 1 effect each falsify the corresponding claim.

Limitations. Sites and kinase are measurements. Ranking before allele replacement limits false negatives from redundant nucleoporin phosphorylation. Phospho-mimetics omit kinase timing and localization. Cultured neurons compress years-long human disease, and TDP-43-model results stay specific to that context. The design tests preclinical necessity and order.

Ranked proposal:
Provisional Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy.
